searchText: What is `v` in an Ethereum prefixed signed message? Is it the y parity bit plus 27? AKA: `recovery_parameter + 27`? From https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-155: > `{0,1} + CHAIN_ID * 2 + 35` where `{0,1}` is the parity of the `y` That is for transactions, I'm trying to sign a message. ohhh, sorry I did find the answer, `y_parity + 27` was the magic. > The currently existing signature scheme using v = 27 and v = 28 remains valid and continues to operate under the same rules as it did previously. From the same EIP, v = 27/28 is the old scheme, yes. And messages seem to use that old one

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
From https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-155:
> `{0,1} + CHAIN_ID * 2 + 35` where `{0,1}` is the parity of the `y`

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: That is for transactions, I'm trying to sign a message.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I did find the answer, `y_parity + 27` was the magic.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
> The currently existing signature scheme using v = 27 and v = 28 remains valid and continues to operate under the same rules as it did previously.
From the same EIP, v = 27/28 is the old scheme, yes. And messages seem to use that old one
